_comment: Machine-owned gate baseline. Read and written by
scripts/check-quality-ratchet.sh. Do NOT restate these numbers in
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, README.md or ROADMAP.md -- prose has nothing
validating it, and the previous AGENTS.md claim of 'Credo strict: 0
issues, Dialyzer clean' was wrong by 1187 and 127 respectively.
Counts may only go down. Lower one, then run with --update.

credo.scope: lib/ src/ test/ web/ apps/ packages/ per .credo.exs
notes: 949 of these 1187 were invisible until packages/ was added to
.credo.exs; the previously reported 238 covered only lib/ test/ web/.
One pass takes ~62 min: mix credo <path> analyzes nothing against this
config, so the scan cannot be sharded by path from the root. Run
nightly. To shard per-PR, give each package its own .credo.exs and run
credo from inside the package.
STALE-HIGH: 1187 was measured before this session's deletions (4,040 lines
of dead code, the SGR and mode-handler forks) and before the palette
consolidation. The next full run should report IMPROVED, not a regression;
lock it in with --gate credo --update. Credo findings arrive on STDOUT
(unlike dialyzer's, which are on STDERR).

dialyzer.scope: root app beams only; packages/ contribute zero findings
notes: 97 = the findings dialyzer actually emits, after .dialyzer_ignore.exs.
Do NOT baseline dialyxir's 'Total errors:' line: it is the count BEFORE
the ignore file is applied. Adding 11 documented palette.ex suppressions
moved 'Skipped: 5' to 'Skipped: 16' and left 'Total errors: 113'
unchanged, so a ratchet reading that line cannot see a suppression land.
History on this metric: 127 raw / 5 skipped = 122 emitted at scan start;
111 raw / 5 skipped = 106 emitted after the a11y_node callback fix removed
16 callback_type_mismatch; 97 emitted after 11 palette.ex contract_supertype
warnings were suppressed as documented intentionally-broad public specs.
MEASUREMENT TRAP: dialyxir keys its deps PLT off the deps hash, which a
path-dependency change does not move. Editing or adding a module under
packages/ leaves the PLT describing the old code, and a fix can read as a
no-op across full runs. check-quality-ratchet.sh refuses to report a count
when any packages/*/lib source is newer than the PLT.
